characters.description: The Dragon Reborn and Car'a'carn, hardened and increasingly isolated, ruling many nations and commanding both the Aiel and a growing corps of Asha'man, with Aes Sedai now sworn to him. Driving grimly toward the Last Battle, he wrestles with the taint's slow madness, trusts almost no one, and means to hunt down the Forsaken one by one.
characters.name: Rand al'Thor

characters.description: Rand's luck-blessed friend, a brilliant reluctant general carrying dead men's memories of war, a Power-turning medallion, and a black-hafted spear. Sent on the Dragon's errands, he grumbles at every turn while proving uncannily good at surviving, and at winning, the trouble fate keeps handing him.
characters.name: Mat Cauthon

characters.description: Rand's steady friend, a wolfbrother and lord of the Two Rivers, wed to Faile and serving at the Dragon's side. Deliberate and loyal, he grows uneasy at how cold and dangerous Rand has become, and torn between duty to his friend and to his wife.
characters.name: Perrin Aybara

characters.description: The innkeeper's daughter of Emond's Field, raised Amyrlin Seat of the rebel Aes Sedai who oppose Elaida. Young in years but iron-willed and cunning, she is steadily out-maneuvering the older sisters who expected to rule through her, and bending them toward war on the usurped White Tower.
characters.name: Egwene al'Vere

characters.description: The former Wisdom of Emond's Field, a channeler of great strength and a gifted Healer, newly wed to Lan and finally learning to reach the Power without her old crutch of anger. Proud and headstrong, she throws herself into the search for a means to mend the broken weather.
characters.name: Nynaeve al'Meara

characters.description: The Daughter-Heir of Andor, a strong channeler working with Nynaeve and Aviendha in the city of Ebou Dar. Poised and dutiful, she pursues an ancient object of the Power while her thoughts turn toward claiming the throne of Andor that is hers by right.
characters.name: Elayne Trakand

characters.description: The uncrowned last king of a fallen Borderland realm and a matchless swordsman, now Warder and husband to Nynaeve. Grim and devoted, he guards her through the dangers of a strange southern city, his fatalism tempered a little by an unexpected marriage.
characters.name: Lan

characters.description: A blunt young woman who foresees the future in images only she can see, now constantly at Rand's side as one of the very few he wholly trusts. Practical and warm beneath a sharp tongue, she has grown close and dear to the Dragon Reborn.
characters.name: Min

characters.description: An Aiel woman training to be a Wise One and a channeler, proud, blunt, and bound by strict honor. Deeply entangled with Rand and with the wetlander customs she still finds baffling, she works alongside Elayne and Nynaeve on their urgent errand.
characters.name: Aviendha

characters.description: A legendary Aes Sedai of fearsome reputation and great age, long thought retired, who reappears with designs of her own concerning the Dragon Reborn and the young men who channel. Blunt, imperious, and cleverer than nearly anyone around her, she is accustomed to bending others to her will without apology.
characters.name: Cadsuane

characters.description: One of the Forsaken, the Dark One's ancient champions, a proud and ruthless war-captain who has seized rule of the nation of Illian under a false name. Jealous of standing among his own kind and contemptuous of the upstart Dragon Reborn, he schemes against Rand from his stronghold.
characters.name: Sammael

recaps.ending: Rand ends the unnatural heat and the Forsaken who most immediately opposed him, but at a cost. He lures Sammael, who has ruled Illian in disguise, into the cursed ruins of Shadar Logoth and leaves him to the hungry evil of Mashadar, then claims Illian and is crowned with its ancient Laurel Crown, the crown of swords. In Ebou Dar, Elayne, Nynaeve, and Aviendha, working with the runaway channelers of the Kin and the sea folk's Windfinders, manage to use the Bowl of the Winds to break the Dark One's grip on the weather and start the seasons turning again. But their triumph is swallowed by disaster: the Seanchan launch an assault on Ebou Dar as the group flees, and Mat is caught beneath a collapsing wall, his fate left uncertain. Meanwhile the formidable Aes Sedai Cadsuane has attached herself to Rand and his Asha'man, meaning to guide, or master, the Dragon Reborn on her own terms. And at the height of his success Rand is ambushed by Padan Fain, whose cursed dagger opens a second wound that crosses and worsens the one he already bears, an injury the Power cannot heal. Rand stands crowned and stronger than ever, the weather mended and a Forsaken dead, yet sicker, warier, and more surrounded by hidden agendas than before, as the Seanchan advance and the Last Battle draws nearer.
recaps.in_short: The Dark One's touch has locked the world in a killing, unnatural heat, and Rand means to end it and to strike at the Forsaken Sammael, who rules the nation of Illian under a false name. In the city of Ebou Dar, Elayne, Nynaeve, Aviendha, and Mat search for the Bowl of the Winds, an ancient object that can mend the weather, working with a hidden society of runaway channelers and the sea folk's Windfinders. Rand, hardening under the strain of command and the taint on the Power, gathers Aes Sedai sworn to him and draws the notice of Cadsuane, a legendary sister with plans of her own. Rand lures Sammael into the cursed ruins of Shadar Logoth and leaves him to the evil that haunts the place, then takes Illian and its crown. The women succeed in working the Bowl, breaking the deadly heat and turning the seasons back toward their course, but as they escape, the Seanchan storm Ebou Dar, and Mat is caught in the collapse. Rand, crowned and victorious, is ambushed by Padan Fain and dealt a second wound that will not heal.

recaps.text: Rand al'Thor, a shepherd of the Two Rivers, was named the Dragon Reborn after he first channeled the One Power: the champion prophesied to fight the Dark One and, because he wields the tainted male Power, fated to go mad. He fought the fiery-eyed enemy in the sky above Falme, was proclaimed the Dragon before the world, drew the crystal sword Callandor from the Stone of Tear, and was accepted by the Aiel as their Car'a'carn after uncovering their hidden past. Leading the Aiel down into the heartland, he destroyed the Forsaken Rahvin at Caemlyn, though the Aes Sedai Moiraine sacrificed herself to remove another Forsaken. Rand came to rule Cairhien, Tear, and Andor, gathered men who can channel into a private army called the Asha'man, and survived a kidnapping by treacherous Aes Sedai, freed at the Battle of Dumai's Wells, after which a number of sisters knelt and swore fealty to him. Along the way Mat became a gifted battle commander; Perrin wed Faile and was made lord of the Two Rivers; Nynaeve and Elayne captured a Forsaken and learned to Heal the once-incurable severing of the gift; Nynaeve married Lan; and Egwene was raised Amyrlin of the rebel Aes Sedai gathered at Salidar, proving far shrewder than her elders expected. As this book opens the Dark One's touch has locked the land in unnatural, blistering heat, the Seanchan press inland, and Rand, hardening and ever more alone, prepares to hunt down the Forsaken who still oppose him.

characters.description: The exiled Targaryen queen and mother of three dragons, who has taken and now rules the great slaver city of Meereen. Determined to break the trade in human beings, she struggles with the grinding work of governing a hostile, foreign city, a shadowy insurgency, and dragons growing too large and dangerous to control.
characters.name: Daenerys Targaryen

characters.description: Eddard Stark's bastard son, now the young Lord Commander of the Night's Watch. Trying to prepare the Wall for the true enemy gathering in the far north, he makes hard and unpopular choices, including dealings with the wildlings, that set many of his own sworn brothers against him.
characters.name: Jon Snow

characters.description: The dwarf Lannister, a hunted fugitive across the sea after murdering his father and fleeing the kingdom he can never return to. Bitter, drunken, and grieving, he sells his wits to survive as he is swept eastward through the free cities toward the distant dragon queen.
characters.name: Tyrion Lannister

characters.description: The crippled Stark boy, traveling far beyond the Wall with a small band of companions in search of a mysterious teacher glimpsed in his dreams. He has begun to sense a strange power waking in himself, tied to the old gods and the weirwood trees.
characters.name: Bran Stark

characters.description: King Robert's stern brother, encamped at the Wall with his dwindling army and still claiming the Iron Throne by right. He looks to win the North to his cause, undeterred by cold, hunger, or the long odds against him, with the priestess Melisandre at his side.
characters.name: Stannis Baratheon

characters.description: The low-born, honest knight who serves Stannis Baratheon as his most trusted and plain-spoken hand. Sent out on a perilous errand to win northern lords to his king's cause, he must trade in words and loyalties rather than swords.
characters.name: Davos Seaworth

characters.description: The disgraced queen mother, imprisoned by the militant Faith on charges of adultery and treason and stripped of her power in the capital. Awaiting judgment in a cell, she nurses her humiliation and her hatred and searches for any way back to authority.
characters.name: Cersei Lannister

characters.description: An aged, legendary knight once the finest blade of the Kingsguard, cast off by the boy king Joffrey and since sworn to the service of Daenerys Targaryen. Honorable and skilled beyond his years, he advises and guards the young queen in her troubled city.
characters.name: Barristan Selmy

characters.description: A disgraced northern knight who fled the realm years ago and became one of Daenerys Targaryen's earliest and most devoted followers, though he was banished from her side when his old secret dealings came to light. Hard, resourceful, and still hopelessly loyal, he seeks a way to redeem himself in her eyes.
characters.name: Jorah Mormont

characters.description: Once the proud heir to the Iron Islands who betrayed the Starks and seized Winterfell, now a broken and terrorized prisoner of House Bolton, so unmanned by torment that he answers to a servant's name and scarcely dares remember who he was. He is a hollow, fearful shell of the young man he had been.
characters.name: Theon Greyjoy

characters.description: The cruel, unpredictable son of Lord Roose Bolton, the northern lord who helped destroy the Starks. Sadistic and dangerous, delighting in the fear and pain of those in his power, he is a menace even to his father's allies as House Bolton tightens its grip on the North.
characters.name: Ramsay Bolton

recaps.ending: The book closes on a string of cliffhangers. Jon Snow, having pushed his hard choices too far, is set upon and stabbed by a group of his own sworn brothers in a mutiny at the Wall, and falls apparently dying in the snow. Daenerys, borne away by her dragon Drogon, is stranded on the vast Dothraki sea, sick and alone, and comes face to face with a mounted khalasar, her fate uncertain; behind her, the old knight Barristan Selmy takes command of a Meereen teetering toward war. Tyrion, alive and sardonic, ends among the sellswords of the Second Sons, plotting his next move toward the dragon queen. Cersei, after a degrading walk of atonement through the capital, is freed from her cell to await a trial by combat, defended by a monstrous, silent new champion. At Winterfell, Theon Greyjoy and the false Stark bride leap from the castle walls to escape Ramsay Bolton and flee toward Stannis, whose army struggles through the snows nearby with battle imminent. Bran Stark, safe beneath the earth, has become a greenseer in training. And in the far south a bold young invader claiming Targaryen blood lands with a seasoned army, opening a wholly new front in the endless contest for the throne.
recaps.in_short: Jon Snow, as Lord Commander, gambles on peace with the wildlings and lets them pass south through the Wall to save them from the coming enemy, a choice that enrages his brothers. Daenerys, besieged by insurgents in Meereen, marries a local nobleman to buy peace and reopens the fighting pits, but when her great dragon Drogon descends in blood and fire she flees the city on his back and ends up lost and starving on the open grasslands, found by a Dothraki horde. Tyrion is swept east, falling in with exiles escorting a mysterious young man who claims a lost royal name, then is captured, enslaved, and finally schemes his way into a sellsword company outside Meereen. Bran reaches his teacher, an ancient greenseer beneath a hollow hill, and begins to see through the eyes of trees and beasts. At Winterfell, the broken captive Theon is forced to serve at the wedding of a false Stark bride to the sadistic Ramsay Bolton, until a flicker of his old self drives him to flee with the girl into the snow. Stannis marches on Winterfell through a killing blizzard as a great new claimant lands in the south with an army.

recaps.text: Previously: The war set off by Eddard Stark's execution broke the realm. By the end of A Storm of Swords, Robb Stark and his mother Catelyn were slain at the Red Wedding, the boy king Joffrey was poisoned, and Tyrion Lannister killed his father Tywin and fled into exile. Jon Snow became Lord Commander of the Night's Watch with Stannis Baratheon at the Wall; Bran Stark traveled beyond it seeking a hidden teacher; and Daenerys Targaryen conquered the eastern slaver cities and settled to rule Meereen. This volume runs alongside the events of A Feast for Crows, so its threads also matter here: in the south, Cersei Lannister's paranoid regency for her son Tommen unraveled after she rearmed the militant Faith, which then imprisoned her on charges of adultery and treason. Jaime Lannister grew estranged from his sister and set out to end the river wars. Sansa Stark remained hidden in the Vale under the schemer Petyr Baelish, while Arya Stark trained among the servants of a death god in Braavos and was struck blind as a test. The ruthless Euron Greyjoy seized the crown of the Iron Islands and looked outward to conquest.

characters.description: One of the last Antari, blood magicians able to step between parallel Londons. Raised inside the Red London palace beside the prince, he serves the Maresh crown as its official messenger, carrying letters between the rulers of the worlds still open to travel. One of his eyes is solid black, the mark of what he is. Reserved, stubborn and quietly resentful of being treated as both a prince and a possession, he keeps a habit that is forbidden in every world: smuggling small objects across for collectors who cannot travel themselves. His coat can be turned inside out into a different coat for each city he walks in.
characters.name: Kell

characters.description: A thief and cutpurse in Grey London, the world that has forgotten magic. She dresses as a boy, carries a good knife and a stolen pistol, and rents a room above a tavern when she can pay for it. She grew up on the street, trusts no one, and wants one thing above all: a ship of her own and the freedom to sail it. Reckless to the point of enjoying danger, she is drawn to anything that suggests the world is larger than the one she was born into.
characters.name: Delilah Bard

characters.description: The heir to the throne of Red London, raised alongside Kell and treated by him as a brother. Charming, indulgent and openly fond of pleasure, he covers a shortage of magical talent with wit and good manners. He is genuinely devoted to Kell and just as genuinely careless with him.
characters.name: Rhy Maresh

characters.description: The ruler of Red London and Rhy's father, who took Kell into the palace as a small child and raised him as a second son. He values Kell's rare ability as an asset of the crown at least as much as he values Kell himself.
characters.name: King Maxim Maresh

characters.description: Rhy's mother and the queen of Red London. She is fond of Kell in a careful, distant way, and uneasy with the power he carries in her household.
characters.name: Queen Emira Maresh

characters.description: The only other living Antari, and the messenger of White London, the starving world where magic must be forced rather than asked. Worn thin and joyless, he is bound by a spell cut into his skin to obey whoever holds his city's throne, and he carries out its rulers' orders without hope of anything better. He tells Kell without malice that the only real difference between them is where each of them happened to be born.
characters.name: Holland

characters.description: One of the twin rulers of White London, who took the throne by killing the pair who held it before. He controls people through binding spells carved into their skin, and appears to enjoy the control itself more than anything it wins him.
characters.name: Athos Dane

characters.description: Athos's twin and the other half of White London's rule, colder and more patient than her brother, and more interested in what might still be taken from a world whose magic is nearly spent.
characters.name: Astrid Dane

characters.description: The keeper of a Grey London tavern who rents Lila a room and puts up with her comings and goings. He is one of the very few people who has ever shown her steady kindness without asking for anything back.
characters.name: Barron

characters.description: A wealthy young Grey Londoner convinced that magic is real, who pays Kell for small enchanted objects smuggled out of the other worlds. He is enthusiastic, harmless and entirely out of his depth.
characters.name: Ned Tuttle

characters.description: The head priest of the London Sanctuary in Red London, an old man who can read the balance of a person's magic at a glance. He is one of the few people Kell will actually listen to, and what he counsels is restraint.
characters.name: Tieren Serense

characters.description: The ailing king of Grey London, whom Kell visits to deliver the monthly letters from the other crowns. He is the one person in his world who knows Kell is real, and nobody around him believes a word of it.
characters.name: King George III

recaps.ending: In White London, Lila kills Athos Dane and Kell breaks the binding spell that has held Holland in service, but Astrid has already crossed into Red London and taken Prince Rhy's body for her own. Kell is forced to destroy her, which means killing his brother, and then uses Antari blood magic to tie his own life to Rhy's so that Rhy lives again; from that moment the two of them share pain, and Rhy cannot die while Kell survives. With Holland mortally wounded, Kell binds the black stone into him and pushes him through the door into Black London, then seals the passage with his blood, putting the stone beyond reach at the cost of the man who carried it. Red London survives with its heir restored and its crown unaware of what the rescue actually cost. Kell's bond with Rhy is a secret that binds them both, and his freedom to travel is now something the king intends to control. Lila, offered a place, chooses the sea instead: she leaves for a ship and a life of her own in a world where magic is real. Holland is presumed dead in a world nothing can enter.
recaps.in_short: Four Londons occupy the same point in different worlds: Grey London has forgotten magic, Red London thrives on it, White London starves for it, and Black London was consumed by it and sealed away. Only Antari, marked by one solid black eye, can travel between them. Kell, one of two living Antari, serves the Red London crown as its messenger and smuggles trinkets on the side. Handed a black stone that turns out to be a fragment of Black London's magic, he is hunted for it, robbed of it in Grey London by a thief named Delilah Bard, and forced into an alliance with her to carry it back where it came from. The stone grants what its holder asks and takes something in return, and the rulers of White London want it. Kell and Lila fight their way through White London, but Astrid Dane reaches Red London first and takes Prince Rhy's body. Kell kills her, binds his own life to Rhy's to save him, and sends the stone into Black London inside the dying Holland before sealing the door. Lila leaves for a ship of her own.

recaps.text: Four Londons sit stacked on the same spot in different worlds. Grey London has forgotten that magic exists; Red London is rich with it; White London is a hard, cold place where a dying magic must be taken by force; and Black London was consumed by magic and sealed off long ago, so completely that its name is barely spoken. Only Antari, blood magicians marked by a single solid black eye, can pass between them. Kell is one of two living Antari. He was brought into the Red London palace as a small child and raised beside Prince Rhy, and he serves the Maresh crown as its official messenger, carrying letters between the rulers of the three worlds still open. He also breaks the law he is meant to uphold, smuggling small objects across the boundaries for collectors who can never travel themselves. In Grey London, meanwhile, a thief named Delilah Bard robs a carriage at knifepoint. She has grown up on the street, dresses as a boy, and wants a ship of her own more than she wants safety.

Kell's rounds take him first to Grey London, where he delivers the crown's letters to an ailing King George, who is the only person in that world who knows what Kell is, and sells a small enchanted stone to Ned Tuttle, an eager young collector. He then crosses to White London, a grey and brutal city ruled by the twins Athos and Astrid Dane, who hold power by fear and keep the world's other Antari, Holland, bound to their service by a spell carved into his skin. Holland tells Kell plainly that the difference between their two lives is luck and nothing else. On his way out of the city, a stranger presses a package on Kell as payment for a delivery. Inside is a black stone marked with an unfamiliar symbol, and the magic in it does not belong to any of the three worlds still standing. It is a piece of Black London, and Kell has just carried it home.

Kell realizes what the stone is and finds that he cannot simply be rid of it: it does what its holder asks and takes something in return, and it does not want to be put down. Word of it moves faster than he does. Attacked in Red London and unable to explain himself to the crown without admitting to years of smuggling, he crosses into Grey London to get the stone out of a living world, and there Delilah Bard picks his pocket and takes it. She has no idea what she has stolen, only that it is worth something, and when she tests it the stone answers her. Kell hunts her down through Grey London while the people who want the stone hunt them both.

Kell finds Lila and, after a short and hostile negotiation, the two of them end up working together: she will not give the stone back and he cannot leave without it. Holland arrives in Grey London under orders to bring the stone to the Danes, and the hunt turns lethal for anyone standing near either of them. Lila, who has spent her life wanting a bigger world, now has proof that there are three more of them, and she refuses to be left behind. She and Kell escape together with the stone, and Kell brings her across into Red London, which no one from her world has any business seeing.

In Red London, Kell and Lila conclude that the stone cannot be destroyed by any magic they have, and that the only place it can safely go is back to Black London, through a door no one has opened in centuries. The stone keeps working on whoever holds it, offering exactly what that person most wants, and the hunt for it has already cost Lila the closest thing she had to a friend in her own world: Barron, the tavern keeper who gave her a room, is dead. Rhy is at the center of the danger without being told why, the crown's guard is closing on Kell, and the Danes are not going to stop. Kell decides to carry the stone to White London himself and end the matter at its source, and Lila, who has no intention of being sent home, goes with him.

White London is worse than Kell described it, and the Danes are ready for them. Kell is taken and held by Athos, who is expert at making a bound person obey, and the stone changes hands. Lila, underestimated because she is a Grey Londoner with no magic to speak of, gets close enough to Athos to put a knife in him and kills him. With Athos dead, Kell is able to break the spell that has held Holland in service for years, though Holland has little left to be grateful with. The victory is incomplete: Astrid is not in her city. She has already crossed into Red London, and she went for the one person Kell would trade anything to protect.

Kell and Lila return to Red London to find that Astrid Dane has taken Prince Rhy's body as her own, intending to trade a dying world for a living one. Kell has no way to drive her out and no way to spare his brother: to kill her he has to kill Rhy. He does it, and then uses Antari blood magic to bind his own life to Rhy's, dragging him back. Rhy lives, but the two of them now share pain and Rhy cannot die while Kell survives, a bond neither the king nor the queen knows about. With Holland mortally wounded, Kell binds the black stone into him and pushes him through the door into Black London, then seals the passage with his own blood, putting the stone beyond anyone's reach at the cost of the man who carried it. Red London keeps its heir and never learns the price. Kell's travelling is now something the crown means to control, and Lila, offered a place in a world full of magic, chooses instead to leave for a ship and a life of her own.

characters.description: A senior at the Scholomance, born to a Welsh healer and a father from an Indian wizarding family who died before she was born. Her magical affinity runs toward destruction and death on a catastrophic scale, and a family prophecy warns that she will bring ruin to the enclaves, so she deliberately starves that talent and gets by on stubbornness and painstakingly earned craft. Prickly, poor, and unaffiliated with any enclave, she resents the students who coast on inherited power while she scrapes for every scrap of mana. She goes by El rather than Galadriel.
characters.name: El

characters.description: A boy from the New York enclave with a rare gift for sensing and killing maleficaria, the monsters that hunt students throughout the school. He has spent years saving classmates almost compulsively, which has made him the closest thing the Scholomance has to a celebrity. When he keeps rescuing El, she is more irritated than grateful, convinced his heroics are wrecking the reputation she has worked to protect. Earnest and a little lost when he is not fighting, he finds her hostility oddly refreshing.
characters.name: Orion Lake

characters.description: An artificer with a practical, deal-making streak, skilled at building and repairing magical objects. She becomes one of the first students willing to treat El as a possible ally rather than a threat, trading favors and eventually agreeing to help craft a graduation weapon with her. Level-headed and quietly generous, she anchors the small circle of independent students forming around El.
characters.name: Aadhya

characters.description: An independent student from a large Chinese wizarding family, talented with music and with the mice she keeps as familiars. Under pressure to succeed for relatives who pooled their resources to send her, she has drifted toward the tempting shortcut of dark magic, but her growing friendship with El and Aadhya helps pull her back from it. Reserved and watchful, she proves a steady partner in their graduation alliance.
characters.name: Liu

characters.description: A student of the New York enclave and one of Orion's friends, accustomed to the security that enclave membership and shared power reserves provide. Her easy assumptions about El cause friction at first, but through her El gets a real look at how enclave privilege works from the inside, and the two slowly begin to see each other differently.
characters.name: Chloe

characters.description: El's mother, a gentle and widely loved healer who raised her in a Welsh commune far from any enclave. She refuses to use dark magic on principle and has always urged El toward the same restraint, even as El's frightening affinity strains against that teaching. Though absent from the school, her love and her example shape every hard choice El makes there.
characters.name: Gwen Higgins

recaps.ending: By the close, El has survived her junior year with her alliance with Aadhya and Liu sealed for the graduation run still a year away, and a warmer but still wary connection to New York's enclave through Chloe Rasmussen - a useful tie, not yet a sealed ally. The year's defining feats are hers: alone, she destroyed a maw-mouth, one of the devouring horrors even enclave wizards can only flee, a kill almost no living wizard can claim, and in the year-end crisis over the graduation hall's failing cleansing machinery she joined the repair effort and unleashed a working that revealed the terrifying scale of the affinity she has spent her life suppressing. Her standing has shifted from feared outcast to someone formidable and worth courting. She has still not touched malia, holding to that line even when it would be easy. She holds the Golden Stone sutras, a working that promises to build an enclave without the usual hidden cost, though she has not yet grasped what that cost is. Her friendship with Orion has become something warmer and harder to name, which makes the final beat land hard: as the new freshmen are inducted, a message from her mother, Gwen, reaches El with a single instruction - stay away from Orion Lake. She is left with no explanation, an alliance to keep alive, a senior year to survive, and a warning she does not understand about the person who has repeatedly saved her life.
recaps.in_short: El Higgins is a junior at the Scholomance, a school for young wizards that has no teachers and drifts in the void, where monsters called maleficaria hunt the students and the only way out is a graduation-day run through a hall full of them. Born with an affinity for spells of mass destruction, she refuses the dark magic that would make them easy, and as a poor, unaffiliated girl she has no enclave to shield her. When New York's celebrated Orion Lake keeps saving her life, it costs her the trust of the other students, but she slowly turns classmates into real allies, chiefly the artificer Aadhya and the musician Liu, and settles into an uneasy friendship with Orion. Over the year she uncovers how the enclaves hoard safety, and acquires the Golden Stone sutras, a spell said to build an enclave without its usual hidden cost. She does what almost no wizard can, destroying a maw-mouth alone, and in the year-end crisis helps repair the graduation hall's failing defenses, remaking her reputation from outcast to someone formidable. The book closes as a warning arrives from her mother: keep away from Orion Lake.

recaps.text: El Higgins is grinding through her junior year at the Scholomance, a school with no teachers that hangs in the void and constantly tries to kill its students with maleficaria, monsters that seep in through the vents, drains, and library shelves to feed on young wizards and their magic. El was born with an affinity for large-scale destruction, spells of devastating power that come to her easily, but she refuses to fuel her magic with malia, the corrupting force drawn from other living things, and insists on the slower, cleaner path of mana earned through effort. Poor and unaffiliated, with no enclave to buy her safety, she survives on grit and a sharp tongue. Her mother, Gwen, is a gentle healer in a Welsh commune, which only sets off how prickly and guarded El has become. To her constant irritation, New York's admired Orion Lake keeps rescuing her from mals, and every rescue makes the other students trust her less, since a girl who needs saving looks either weak or, worse, like she is manipulating him. Isolated and defensive, and privately aware that her gift could kill on a horrifying scale if she ever let it, El begins the wary, unglamorous work of turning wary classmates into allies rather than rivals, because no one survives graduation alone.

El's careful alliance-building starts to take real shape. She grows closest to Aadhya, a practical artificer from New Jersey who can build and repair the gear everyone will need, and to Liu, a quiet, musically gifted girl from an independent Chinese wizard family who is distrusted because she keeps mice, which others assume means she dabbles in malia. El, who knows exactly how unfair that kind of suspicion is, chooses to look past it. The daily reality of the school stays brutal: attendance means dodging monsters, guarding your food and water, and weighing every favor as a transaction, since alliances are ultimately negotiations about who will watch whose back when graduation comes. Orion continues to turn up whenever El is in danger, and their mutual annoyance slowly warms toward something like friendship, though El resents needing him and resents more that his heroics keep marking her out. She lets slip, mostly to herself, just how much power she is holding back, and begins to understand that her real problem is not weakness but the constant temptation to solve everything the easy, ruinous way.

As the term wears on, El's loose understandings with Aadhya and Liu firm into a genuine alliance, the first real trust she has allowed herself. The three begin planning in earnest for graduation, pooling skills and thinking about what gear and weapons will carry them through the mal-choked hall that stands between every senior and the outside world. El and Orion drift from open irritation into a real, prickly friendship, and she catches herself relying on him. Meanwhile she keeps studying the shape of the world she is trapped in: how the enclaves, the fortified strongholds of the wealthiest wizard families, hoard mana and safety while independents like her scrape by, and how that inequality follows students right into the school. The ordinary horrors never pause, with monsters massing in the plumbing and the darker corners of the library, and El occasionally lets a glimpse of her true capacity show, enough to unsettle the people around her. Every new bond doubles as a hard bargain about survival, and El, unused to being wanted for anything, navigates it with equal parts suspicion and reluctant hope.

El, Aadhya, and Liu commit to a shared graduation strategy built around a concrete project: after Orion kills an enormous mal called a sirenspider, Aadhya salvages its shell to craft an instrument for Liu, whose music can be shaped into a weapon for the run through the graduation hall. El keeps refusing the shortcut of dark magic even when it would instantly end a deadly problem, and her standing slowly shifts from feared loner toward someone genuinely worth allying with, drawing wary interest even from New York's enclavers. She learns more about how the enclaves are built and sustained, and how much of the wizard world's comfort is quietly bought at the expense of people like her. She also grows uneasy about Orion, whose drive to hunt and destroy monsters is far greater than any ordinary wizard's, an appetite that begins to look less like heroism than like a mystery she cannot name. Around her the school's threat keeps climbing, and El quietly accumulates power, allies, and knowledge, including a book of construction magic that cuts directly against her ruinous affinity and hints that the enclaves' safety need not be built the way it always has been.

As the year's end approaches, the school's dangers come to a head. A student maleficer who had been preying on other students to feed his power is exposed and stopped after turning on El herself, hardening her refusal to ever take that path. El also does what almost no living wizard can claim: alone, she faces a maw-mouth, one of the vast, near-unkillable horrors made of everyone it has swallowed, and destroys it outright, pouring out an enormous store of mana at brutal cost to her reserves and her nerve. When the graduation hall's cleansing machinery proves to be failing, dooming the graduating class above and letting maleficaria leak up into the school, El joins the repair effort, and in the fighting below unleashes a working that helps clear the hall and reveals the terrifying scale of the affinity she has spent her life suppressing. By year's end her standing is remade from pitiable outsider to someone formidable and worth allying with. Her alliance with Aadhya and Liu is sealed for their own graduation run a year away, she has earned a warmer but wary connection to New York through Chloe Rasmussen, and she is closer to Orion than she has let anyone be. That fragile peace breaks with the book's final beat: as the incoming freshmen are inducted, a message reaches her from her mother, Gwen, carrying a single, unexplained warning to keep away from Orion Lake.

characters.description: The widowed queen, now ruling the realm as Queen Regent for her young son, King Tommen, following the deaths of her son Joffrey and her father Tywin. Proud, suspicious, and increasingly untethered, she is determined to hold absolute power and to crush every rival she imagines around her, including her own kin.
characters.name: Cersei Lannister

characters.description: Cersei's twin and Lord Commander of the Kingsguard, still adjusting to the loss of his sword hand and the humbling it brought. Grown weary of his family's cruelties and drifting from his sister, he sets out to bring the war in the river lands to a quiet end and to reconsider the kind of man he wishes to be.
characters.name: Jaime Lannister

characters.description: The tall, plain, and powerfully built warrior woman, earnest and stubbornly honorable, who travels the ravaged countryside on a quest to find and protect the lost Stark daughter Sansa, keeping a promise she means to honor whatever the cost.
characters.name: Brienne of Tarth

characters.description: The elder Stark daughter, hidden in the mountain fastness of the Vale under a false name and passed off as the natural daughter of the schemer Petyr Baelish. Watchful and wary, she is slowly being taught the subtle, dangerous arts of court intrigue by her protector.
characters.name: Sansa Stark

characters.description: The younger Stark daughter, arrived in the free city of Braavos, where she seeks out a mysterious order of assassins who serve a god of death. Fierce and self-contained, she begins to learn their secretive ways while clinging to the memory of who she is.
characters.name: Arya Stark

characters.description: The timid, bookish brother of the Night's Watch and friend of Jon Snow, sent away from the Wall on a long sea voyage south to train as a maester. Frightened of the wider world but loyal and quietly resourceful, he travels with companions entrusted to his care.
characters.name: Samwell Tarly

characters.description: A smooth, ambitious lord of modest origins who has climbed high through cunning, coin, and manipulation. Having taken control of the Vale, he keeps the hidden Sansa Stark close as his supposed daughter and plays a patient, layered game whose true aims he reveals to no one.
characters.name: Petyr Baelish

characters.description: The young, gracious, and popular queen of the powerful House Tyrell, now wed to the boy king Tommen after the deaths of her previous royal betrotheds. Charming and politically deft, she and her family are viewed by the queen mother Cersei as dangerous rivals for influence over the crown.
characters.name: Margaery Tyrell

characters.description: A dreaded ironborn captain and brother to the late lord of the Iron Islands, long exiled for his crimes and returned by sea to press a claim to rule his people. Cruel, cunning, and rumored to dabble in dark and foreign sorceries, he is a man other hard men fear.
characters.name: Euron Greyjoy

recaps.ending: Cersei Lannister's grasping regency ends in disaster. Having empowered the militant Faith to strike at her enemies, she is herself denounced for adultery and treason and thrown into a cell to await the Faith's judgment, stripped of power and abandoned. Her plea for help reaches Jaime, who reads her letter and coldly refuses, choosing to burn it and turn away, the breach between the twins now open. Brienne, having tracked the roads in search of Sansa, falls into the hands of a band of vengeful outlaws led by a hanged and revived Catelyn Stark, and is given a brutal choice between a sword and a noose, screaming a single word as the volume closes. Sansa remains hidden in the Vale, growing more capable under Baelish's tutelage. Arya, having killed on the order of her mysterious masters, is struck blind as a test of her devotion. Samwell reaches the southern city of Oldtown to begin his maester's training, though the ancient Maester Aemon dies on the journey. The ironborn, now led by the ruthless Euron Greyjoy, look outward toward conquest, and the realm settles into an uneasy, exhausted lull with no true peace in sight.
recaps.in_short: With the great war largely spent, the survivors scramble amid the wreckage. Queen Cersei, ruling as regent for her young son Tommen, grows ever more paranoid, turning on allies and kin alike. To undercut her rivals, she rearms the religious militants of the Faith and empowers their austere leader, a decision that swiftly rebounds upon her. Jaime, sickened by his sister, rides into the river lands to bring the last sieges to a bloodless close and drifts further from her. Brienne of Tarth roams the ruined countryside searching for Sansa, who is in truth hidden in the Vale, being schooled in intrigue by Petyr Baelish. In Braavos, Arya begins her strange apprenticeship among the servants of a death god. On the Iron Islands, the ironborn hold a kingsmoot after their lord's death, and the fearsome exile Euron Greyjoy seizes the crown of salt and rock. In Dorne, a plot to crown a young princess collapses in blood. Cersei's schemes finally trap her: accused of adultery and treason, she is seized and imprisoned by the very Faith she armed.

recaps.text: Previously: Eddard Stark's execution and his son Robb's rise as King in the North set off a war among rival claimants to the Iron Throne. By the end of A Storm of Swords the Stark cause lay in ruins. Robb Stark and his mother Catelyn were butchered at the treacherous Red Wedding. The boy king Joffrey was poisoned at his own wedding feast; his brother Tommen was crowned in his place, with Cersei Lannister ruling as regent. Tyrion Lannister, wrongly condemned for Joffrey's murder, killed his father Tywin and fled into exile. Jaime Lannister returned to the capital maimed, having lost his sword hand. Sansa Stark was hidden away in the Vale by Petyr Baelish under a false name, while Arya Stark took ship for the free city of Braavos. Jon Snow, having repelled a wildling assault at the Wall, was chosen Lord Commander of the Night's Watch, with Stannis Baratheon encamped nearby. Daenerys Targaryen conquered the eastern slaver cities and settled to rule in Meereen. This volume follows the aftermath in the south and the west, while other threads unfold elsewhere at the same time.

characters.description: A university professor, Red Guard consultant, and Sebastien's mentor. He studies the Raven Queen while negotiating access to a protected archaeological project, approaching both investigations as routes to otherwise restricted knowledge.
characters.name: Thaddeus Lacer

characters.description: A university history-department grandmaster who summons Thaddeus Lacer, questions him about the Raven Queen investigation, and controls access to protected archaeological material. The grandmaster offers information in exchange for Lacer's cooperation and secrecy.
characters.name: History-department grandmaster

characters.description: A gifted university thaumaturge and Thaddeus Lacer's apprentice. During a defensive practical, Sebastien becomes the group's strategist, combining adaptable spellwork with a strong preference for keeping teammates alive.
characters.name: Sebastien Siverling

characters.description: Sebastien's trusted classmate and defensive-magic teammate. Damien contributes scouting and camouflage tools while following Sebastien's tactical lead.
characters.name: Damien Westbay

characters.description: A member of the Gervin family and one of Sebastien's allies. Anna responds to the defensive-practical alarm by helping contain damaging gossip and offering practical social support.
characters.name: Anna Gervin

characters.description: Anna's younger sister and another ally of Sebastien. Natalia joins Anna in planning a response to rumors after the university mistakes Sebastien's unusual conduit technique for dangerous magic, helping protect Sebastien's standing among the students.
characters.name: Natalia Gervin

characters.description: A covert contact who passes along Thaddeus Lacer's request for a meeting with the Raven Queen. Oliver protects Sebastien's invented history while pursuing interests of his own, leaving her dependent on assistance whose full purpose she cannot safely assume.
characters.name: Oliver Dryden

characters.description: An independent thaumaturge whom Oliver regards as trustworthy but not necessarily honorable. Sebastien considers Liza a possible custodian for sensitive property, yet remains unwilling to rely on her completely.
characters.name: Liza

characters.description: Damien's brother and the Lord Commander of the Coppers. Titus investigates Sebastien's background, her connection to Damien, and her association with Oliver, making him an official obstacle to her secrecy.
characters.name: Titus Westbay

characters.description: Siobhan is Sebastien Siverling beneath a set of magical disguises and public identities. She uses these presentations to conduct covert work, negotiate through intermediaries, and keep the wanted Raven Queen separate from her university life.
characters.name: Siobhan

characters.description: A prognose woman attached to Lord Linwood's household and Millennium's mother. She agrees to deliver a covert letter and create a public distraction in exchange for a future spell meant to let her son sleep safely.
characters.name: Gera

characters.description: Head of the Linwood household and an affiliate of the Nightmare Pack. His home shelters Gera and Millennium and provides Siobhan with a discreet place to arrange services, communicate with trusted intermediaries, and appear as the Raven Queen.
characters.name: Lord Linwood

characters.description: Gera's fae-blooded son, troubled by predictive visions that disrupt his sleep. Millennium meets Siobhan at Lord Linwood's home, where she offers practical comfort while owing his mother a more durable solution.
characters.name: Millennium Linwood

characters.description: Sebastien's imprisoned father. Sebastien expects his approaching sentencing to give the Coppers an occasion to renew their attempt to locate the Raven Queen.
characters.name: Ennis Nott

characters.description: A university contact whom Sebastien approaches for a discreet meeting, expecting Tanya to recognize an unsigned request without attracting attention.
characters.name: Tanya Canelo

characters.description: A severely malnourished orphan whom Sebastien finds ill after eating unsafe food. Sebastien brings Betty to a healer and persuades the Lord Commander to pay for her treatment, overnight care, and short-term aid.
characters.name: Betty

characters.description: Millennium Linwood’s maid, who accompanies him and his protectors while they flee Pendragon operatives.
characters.name: Martha

characters.description: Katerine's nephew and one of the children held with Millennium in a sensory-deprivation prison. Theo is injured but alive when Siobhan finds the captives and begins organizing their escape from guards who are prepared to use lethal force.
characters.name: Theo

characters.description: A Verdant Stag enforcer imprisoned with the abducted civilians. Though badly beaten, Gerard remains able to organize the other captives as Siobhan works to free them, providing order while injuries and renewed attacks threaten the group.
characters.name: Enforcer Gerard

characters.description: A Verdant Stag enforcer gravely injured during the abduction. Turner has a serious broken leg when Siobhan finds him among the captives.
characters.name: Enforcer Turner

characters.description: A Pendragon operative who abandons his former side during the escape. Anders accepts a bargain with Siobhan in exchange for healing and extending the life of his disabled dog, then helps the captives evade the organization he previously served.
characters.name: Anders

characters.description: A defecting Pendragon operative who helps conceal the escape group. Parker worries that association with Siobhan will endanger his daughter and aunt, and seeks protection for them in exchange for further service.
characters.name: Parker

characters.description: A senior Verdant Stag operator and aunt of one of the rescued children. Katerine arrives at the warded arena after learning that the children are safe.
characters.name: Katerine

characters.description: A burned survivor of the abduction and an outspoken follower of the Raven Queen. Deidre plans to collect accounts from the rescued captives, helping turn their incomplete observations into a shared legend.
characters.name: Deidre Johnson

characters.description: Anders’s elderly, gravely injured dog. Siobhan has promised to restore Bear’s health and grant him an exceptionally long life.
characters.name: Bear

characters.description: A Pendragon operative who survives Siobhan's shadow creature entering his body. Healers cannot determine its continuing effect on Jorgensen.
characters.name: Jorgensen

characters.description: Siobhan's short-lived persona for gaining access to Willowdale alongside Liza. The disguise casts her as Liza's relative from Silva Erde and an apprentice healer.
characters.name: Amelia

characters.description: A surviving archaeologist from the Black Wastes expedition. Edgar is paranoid, prone to hallucinations, and detached from his own name, but remains a possible witness to what was recovered from Merton's hermitage.
characters.name: Edgar

characters.description: A university grandmaster connected to the Architects of Khronos. Kiernan seeks Merton's alleged process for converting magical beast cores into usable solarium.
characters.name: Grandmaster Kiernan

characters.description: Anastasia Gervin is Sebastien's ally Anna Gervin. She openly supports and protects Sebastien during a difficult meeting with Oliver Dryden.
characters.name: Anastasia Gervin

characters.description: An unidentified Red Guard operative who confines Siobhan in a distorted space and imposes a three-minute contest with lethal terms. The agent wields a parasitic aberrant flesh glove that can sever physical matter and magical connections.
characters.name: Masked Red Guard agent

recaps.ending: Sebastien survives the High Crown's hostage operation and a Red Guard contest, but both conflicts leave lasting exposure. She keeps her identities separate from the public, acquires a private home and warded resources, opens Merton's journal, and gains the effective raven sleep proxy. Thaddeus Lacer returns her mother's genuine ring and agrees to represent her interests within the Red Guard, while remaining unaware that the being sealed in her memory briefly controlled her detached shadow. Oliver retains a different journal, and their damaged partnership resumes on guarded, more equal terms. Damien continues investigating suppressed Red Guard conduct without knowing Sebastien is the Raven Queen. Liza, Anna, the Nightmare Pack, and the Verdant Stag survivors remain allies with separate obligations. Ennis is free but missing, Edgar has vanished, Parker is dead, and Parker's family has been relocated. Kiernan has stopped answering while an Architects of Khronos team threatens people in Osham. The solarium shortage, the missing fifth journal, the sealed being, Red Guard attention, and the Raven Queen's expanding organized worship all remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Sebastien begins the term under official scrutiny while preparing to break the sympathetic link authorities can use against the Raven Queen. A High Crown operation instead abducts her with children and faction allies, hoping the captives will draw the Raven Queen into a trap. She escapes sensory deprivation, turns two guards, rescues the prisoners, and leads them out, though Parker is captured and later dies. While recovering, she learns that five Merton journals may exist and that one may describe converting beast cores into solarium as natural supplies fail. Oliver admits stealing that journal, fracturing their alliance, while Sebastien eventually opens her own. Her sleep-proxy research succeeds, Ennis escapes, and Damien joins a cautious investigation into Red Guard abuses. A Red Guard contest ends when the being sealed in Sebastien's memory takes control of her detached shadow. Thaddeus Lacer becomes her tentative intermediary and returns her mother's ring. She and Oliver restore limited cooperation, but the Architects' Osham operation and an uncontrolled faith in the Raven Queen remain open.

recaps.text: Previously: Sebastien Siverling established herself as a gifted university thaumaturge while concealing dangerous private work behind several identities. She studies under Thaddeus Lacer and relies on Damien Westbay as a friend and classmate, though Damien does not know the full nature of her secrets. Oliver Dryden protects her invented background and serves as a covert ally, but his political interests make complete trust impossible. Liza works with Sebastien on difficult magical research under similarly guarded terms. Tanya Canelo is entangled with the Architects of Khronos, while Sebastien's father, Ennis Nott, remains imprisoned. Beyond the university, the wanted Raven Queen has become important to the Verdant Stag and Nightmare Pack and remains the target of persistent official investigations. Sebastien also possesses an inaccessible journal recovered from Merton's hermitage. Its changing glyphs have resisted ordinary attempts to read it, leaving both its contents and its connection to wider conflicts unknown.

Thaddeus Lacer joins a protected university effort to unlock archaeological material while seeking contact with the Raven Queen. At the university, Sebastien leads a defensive practical across a simulated city. When she casts through Damien's conduit against her calf, faculty mistake the technique for flesh-casting and halt the examination. Lacer verifies that the difficult method is legitimate, clearing her of an imminent aberrance event. Sebastien then earns exceptional recognition for a complex exhibition and is formally accepted as Lacer's apprentice, though he identifies a weakness in her darkness-focused transmogrification. Official attention remains a separate danger. An investigator questions Damien about Sebastien's connection to Oliver, and Sebastien preserves her cover by supporting Damien's mistaken theory about a secret organization. She asks Damien to compare decades of rogue-magic and Red Guard records for suspicious discrepancies. She also decides to seek a surviving member of the Black Wastes expedition at Willowdale, hoping for a new path toward understanding the journal recovered from Merton's hermitage.

Sebastien fails to decrypt the hidden journal and grows more suspicious of Oliver, whose fabricated history for her has attracted Titus Westbay's investigation. Oliver says the cover still holds, but its invented past needs reinforcement. Sebastien chooses to meet Titus directly rather than wait for him to uncover inconsistencies. Under her alternate identities, she also arranges a letter to the High Crown and bargains with Gera for delivery and a future public distraction, promising a sleep-transfer spell for Millennium in return. With Liza, she begins human trials of a raven-based sleep proxy and plans to destroy the blood sample used by the Coppers to locate the Raven Queen. The operation is meant to coincide with Ennis Nott's sentencing. Sebastien's first-term results are strong, and Lacer helps her select and translate a demanding restorative spell. Her attempt at negotiation fails when the High Crown publicly promises the Raven Queen's capture and execution. Still needing money and assistance, Sebastien develops a selective darkness product, approaches Tanya Canelo for covert work, and begins her meeting with Titus while keeping her larger plan concealed.

Titus acknowledges that he overread the evidence around Sebastien after she pushes him to help a starving orphan, though she intends to avoid him afterward. Sebastien restricts her own access to a substance she fears she depends on, then recruits Tanya to impersonate the Raven Queen from a distance during the sentencing operation. Lacer's work reveals that the protected journals respond to identity and sequences of concepts rather than ordinary ciphers. Sebastien discovers that she can maintain two separate magical wills, passes the journal's two-concept test, and names her counter-scrying plan Operation Palimpsest. She also learns a restorative light technique and locates the recovering expedition survivor at Willowdale, where Liza has an unexplained treatment role. On the sentencing day, Tanya arrives injured after an Architects of Khronos mission lost a dangerous shipment to a military team. Siobhan heals her and proceeds with the plan, but suspects the Coppers have placed a broad compulsion over the city to draw in the Raven Queen. Before she reaches Liza's protection, a Copper stops her in the street.

Millennium helps Siobhan escape the Copper's scrutiny, but Pendragon operatives use him as bait and capture their group with a stun trap. The kidnappers take Siobhan, Millennium, Theo, and members of the Nightmare Pack and Verdant Stag to an underground prison under complete sensory deprivation. Siobhan uses her active will to regain limited awareness, adapts her shadow familiar into a substitute sense, and escapes the deprivation array. Meanwhile, the planned mass of ravens draws the official force away from Ennis's sentencing. Inside the complex, Siobhan frees the other captives but is badly injured by a radiant explosive and confined in a bright cell. Recognizing that concussion and will strain are impairing her judgment, she abandons a reckless escape attempt. Instead, she frightens two guards into bargaining. They agree to neutralize their loyalty vows and help her in exchange for personal boons. The defectors release the prisoners, recover their equipment, and destroy stored blood and hair that could be used for tracking. With reinforcements approaching, Siobhan covers the group in darkness and leads them into an uncertain tunnel route.

Siobhan repairs Enforcer Turner's shattered leg well enough for travel and extends her anti-divination shadow over the fugitives. Anders and Parker, the two defectors, guide the group toward a gulf ferry station. They steal a boat and disable a pursuing vessel, but Parker is harpooned and pulled into Pendragon custody. Thaddeus secretly helps the remaining escapees by killing two pursuers and damaging their boat while concealing his intervention from the authorities. The survivors reach a warded arena, where Liza confirms that the planned operation destroyed the Coppers' usable blood sample. Siobhan is left with serious injuries and will strain. The rescued factions arrange protection while Katerine and Gera treat the kidnapping as an act of war against their families. Siobhan refuses immediate retaliation but asks them to protect the survivors and help honor the boons she promised. Deidre Johnson begins gathering accounts that strengthen the Raven Queen's supernatural reputation. At court, the High Crown confirms that the children were taken to pressure allied factions and lure the Raven Queen. Thaddeus realizes Sebastien was also an intended hostage, while the shadow's unexplained effect on Jorgensen deepens official fear.

While recovering, Siobhan accepts that an unknown presence is sealed within her mind and contacts Thaddeus for information about consciousness held inside memory. Parker is tortured in Crown custody and later dies, leaving Siobhan determined to protect his family. The other abductees and their relatives are successfully hidden or relocated. At Willowdale, Siobhan meets Edgar, the recovering Black Wastes archaeologist. He says the expedition found five Merton journals rather than four and believes a missing volume could be important enough to cause conflict with Osham. Sebastien begins a ritual intended to create an untraceable guiding symbol, but fears its language may be influenced by the sealed presence. She gives Damien a limited account of the abduction, and he accepts that the High Crown committed atrocities while continuing their records research. The new university term begins with Tanya serving as Lacer's student aide. Lacer explains that transmogrification depends on shared cultural associations, revealing why Sebastien's literal thinking has impaired her casting. She learns how to work with that principle, but also discovers that the Red Guard has opened an investigation into whether the Raven Queen poses an exceptional threat.

Sebastien masters output detachment and improves her troubled transmogrification, then confronts Grandmaster Kiernan. He says the Architects of Khronos seek a journal describing how to convert beast cores into solarium because the mines may fail within a decade. Edgar's report of a fifth journal changes the search. Oliver then admits that he arranged the theft of one Merton journal, while Sebastien reveals that she holds another. She accuses him of benefiting from her stolen-book crisis, and their friendship collapses into a pact of mutual secrecy. Sebastien builds independent housing, communications, identities, and warded storage. The Nightmare Pack relocates vulnerable survivors and Parker's family, while Siobhan and Liza use nonlethal vitality transfers to greatly improve Anders's dying dog. Anna confirms that she independently forged her father's signature to block Oliver's contract. Sebastien tells Lacer that she is Siobhan and the Raven Queen and can split her will. Damien commits to cautious research into suspected Red Guard abuses. Liza's raven sleep proxy succeeds, giving Siobhan sustained rest, and Ennis escapes his labor camp. Kiernan and Lacer offer conditional journal cooperation. At last, Sebastien passes the final glyph test and opens her previously unreadable journal.

Merton's journal proves difficult to read even after opening, though it records self-charging artifacts and related lost techniques. The Architects stage a false Raven Queen sighting in Silva Erde, then Tanya warns that one of their teams plans to abduct people in Osham. Oliver tries to contact Kiernan, but no reply arrives. During a renewed sleep-proxy period, a masked Red Guard agent traps Siobhan in a space distorted by supernatural rain and offers a lethal timed contest. The agent's aberrant flesh glove cuts both matter and magical connections, and hidden binding magic turns Siobhan's attacks into worsening cold backlash. When her detached shadow becomes autonomous, the being sealed in her memory uses it to confront the Red Guard and force her escape. The being then withdraws, leaving Siobhan aware that added power and separation from the seal can give it an opening. She seeks help from Thaddeus. He returns her mother's genuine solarium ring, admits replacing it with a dangerous flawed ring, and agrees to serve as her Red Guard intermediary. At Theo's birthday, Sebastien and Oliver restore a guarded alliance based on mutual secrets. Kiernan and the Osham targets remain missing from contact, while organized worship of the Raven Queen spreads beyond Siobhan's control.

characters.description: Lord of Winterfell and Warden of the North, ruler of the vast northern half of the Seven Kingdoms. Stern, plainspoken, and devoted to duty, family, and the old gods of his homeland. Years earlier he helped his friend Robert Baratheon win the throne in rebellion, and he still keeps to the harder, more honest customs of the North. Married to Catelyn Tully, he is father to five trueborn children and guardian of a baseborn son. He prizes honor above ambition and is deeply uneasy with the flattery and scheming of the southern court.
characters.name: Eddard Stark

characters.description: Lady of Winterfell, born to House Tully of Riverrun in the south and wed to Eddard Stark. A strong-willed, capable, and protective mother who keeps the worship of the Seven rather than her husband's old gods. Warm toward her own children but cold toward her husband's bastard, whose presence she has never forgiven. Politically shrewd, she is fiercely loyal to her family and its interests.
characters.name: Catelyn Stark

characters.description: The eldest trueborn son of Eddard and Catelyn Stark and heir to Winterfell. A dutiful, well-trained youth in his mid-teens who carries himself with the seriousness of a boy raised to one day rule the North.
characters.name: Robb Stark

characters.description: Eddard Stark's bastard son, raised at Winterfell beside the trueborn children but always set a little apart by his birth. Close in age and friendship to Robb, quiet and skilled with a blade, he knows a bastard can inherit nothing. He is drawn toward the Night's Watch, the sworn brotherhood that mans the great Wall guarding the realm's far north.
characters.name: Jon Snow

characters.description: The elder Stark daughter, a graceful and courteous girl devoted to songs, courtesy, and the ideals of southern chivalry. She dreams of marrying a gallant highborn prince and becoming a great lady of the court.
characters.name: Sansa Stark

characters.description: The younger Stark daughter, a willful, restless tomboy who prefers riding, adventure, and swordplay to needlework and ladylike manners, and who is often at odds with her prim elder sister.
characters.name: Arya Stark

characters.description: The second Stark son, a boy of seven who loves to scale the walls and towers of Winterfell and dreams of one day growing up to be a knight.
characters.name: Bran Stark

characters.description: King of the Seven Kingdoms, who seized the crown in a rebellion years before with Eddard Stark at his side. Once a mighty warrior and Ned's closest friend, he has grown fat, restless, and weary of the labor of ruling, far fonder of feasting, hunting, and drink than of governance. He is wed, unhappily, to Cersei of House Lannister.
characters.name: Robert Baratheon

characters.description: Queen to King Robert and a proud, beautiful daughter of the immensely wealthy House Lannister of Casterly Rock. Ambitious and watchful, she guards her family's power and her own standing at court with cold intelligence.
characters.name: Cersei Lannister

characters.description: Cersei's dazzling twin brother, a gifted and handsome knight of the Kingsguard. He is known as the Kingslayer for having slain the previous king, the very man he had sworn to protect, during the rebellion that put Robert on the throne, a deed that stains his golden reputation.
characters.name: Jaime Lannister

characters.description: The youngest of the Lannister siblings, a dwarf mocked as the Imp and little loved by his own family. Denied a warrior's stature, he arms himself instead with a sharp tongue, wide reading, and a keen understanding of people, and takes his pleasures in wine and clever talk. He is the cleverest Lannister and the least respected.
characters.name: Tyrion Lannister

characters.description: A young princess of the fallen House Targaryen, the dynasty that once ruled the Seven Kingdoms astride dragons until Robert's rebellion cast it down. Exiled across the narrow sea since infancy, she has lived in poverty and fear under her domineering elder brother Viserys, who clings to the dream of reclaiming the throne. Timid at the outset, she is sold in marriage to a powerful warlord of the nomadic Dothraki to buy her brother an army.
characters.name: Daenerys Targaryen

recaps.ending: Ned Stark is executed on King Joffrey's order despite the mercy he was promised, shattering any hope of peace. His son Robb, declared King in the North, wins his early battles and captures the knight Jaime Lannister, with his mother Catelyn at his side. Sansa remains a captive in King's Landing, betrothed to the boy king who killed her father, while Arya, disguised as a boy, escapes the capital and is carried northward. Crippled Bran and his little brother Rickon remain at Winterfell, and Bran is troubled by vivid wolf-dreams. Jon Snow commits fully to the Night's Watch as unmistakable signs mount that the ancient enemy beyond the Wall is returning. Farthest away, Daenerys Targaryen, widowed and childless after the death of Khal Drogo, steps into his funeral pyre clutching three fossilized dragon eggs and rises from the ashes unburned, three living dragons clinging to her, reborn as a queen with a power the world had thought long dead. The realm has broken into open war, and every side believes itself the rightful one.
recaps.in_short: Lord Eddard Stark leaves Winterfell to serve his friend King Robert as Hand of the King, a post whose previous holder was murdered. Investigating in the capital, Ned learns the deadly secret that Queen Cersei's children are not the king's but were fathered by her own twin brother, Jaime Lannister. Before he can act, Robert dies of a hunting wound, and Cersei's cruel son Joffrey takes the throne. Betrayed by allies he trusted, Ned is arrested and, despite a promise of mercy, publicly beheaded. His son Robb raises the North and is proclaimed King in the North, while Robert's brothers Stannis and Renly each claim the crown too, plunging the realm into war. The Stark family is scattered: Sansa a hostage, Arya fleeing in disguise, Bran crippled and left at Winterfell, and Jon Snow sworn to the Night's Watch as an ancient enemy wakes beyond the Wall. Across the sea, the exiled Daenerys Targaryen loses her warlord husband and unborn child, then walks into his funeral pyre and emerges unburned with three newborn dragons, the first the world has seen in over a century.

recaps.text: The story opens in the North of a land called the Seven Kingdoms, where seasons last for years and a long winter is feared to be coming. Lord Eddard Stark rules the ancient castle of Winterfell as Warden of the North. Far to the north, beyond a colossal ice Wall manned by the sworn brothers of the Night's Watch, something old and cold is beginning to stir in the haunted forest. When the king's chief minister, the Hand of the King, dies unexpectedly, King Robert Baratheon travels north to Winterfell to ask his old friend and comrade Ned to take the dead man's place at court. The Stark children come into possession of a litter of direwolf pups, the sigil of their house. Far across the sea, the last exiled children of the overthrown dragon dynasty scheme to win back the throne their family lost. It is a realm of great houses, old grudges, and looming winter, where a game of thrones is quietly beginning.

characters.description: One of the last Antari, the Red London crown's messenger, and the adopted brother of its heir. Months after the trouble with the black stone he is watched, restricted and blamed: his travelling has been curtailed, the king no longer trusts him with much, and the bond he made to save Rhy means every risk he takes is also someone else's. Restless and increasingly reckless about it, he looks for somewhere to put the part of himself that is not allowed out any more.
characters.name: Kell

characters.description: The Grey London thief who talked her way into a world with magic and then onto a ship. She now sails with a privateer crew, learning the trade and the sea, and hiding how fast her own magic is growing and what her missing eye conceals. She is a quick study, an enthusiastic fighter, and entirely uninterested in going back to being anyone's passenger.
characters.name: Delilah Bard

characters.description: Captain of the Night Spire, a privateer sailing under the Arnesian crown's licence to rob its enemies. Born into a Red London noble house and no longer welcome in it, he is charming, vain, generous with his crew and very good at his work. He sees magic as colored threads around a person, which is how he notices what Lila is trying to keep to herself.
characters.name: Alucard Emery

characters.description: The heir to Red London's throne, who survived what happened to him only because Kell tied their lives together. He cannot die while Kell lives, and he feels everything Kell feels. He has thrown himself into staging a great international magicians' tournament in his city, partly out of genuine ambition and partly to outrun what was done to him.
characters.name: Rhy Maresh

characters.description: The White London Antari, who was pushed through a sealed door into a dead world with a fragment of its magic bound inside him, and who did not die there. Broken, starving and alone in the ruins of Black London, he is found by something that offers to make him whole and to give him back his own ruined city, in exchange for a great deal more than he is being told.
characters.name: Holland

characters.description: The living magic of Black London: a will with no body, ancient and enormously powerful, that speaks in offers and bargains. It is patient, persuasive, and keeps its promises only in the letter. What it wants is what it has always wanted, a world to remake and a body strong enough to carry it into one.
characters.name: Osaron

characters.description: A White London fighter with yellow eyes, raised up out of the city's gutters into something far stronger than she was born as, and loyal to the man who did it. She is sent out of her world to do work that cannot be done openly.
characters.name: Ojka

characters.description: The head priest of the London Sanctuary, who reads the balance of a person's magic at a glance and has known Kell since he was a child. He is one of the few people in the city who treats both Kell and Rhy as people rather than as instruments of the crown.
characters.name: Tieren Serense

characters.description: The king of Red London, who now regards Kell less as a second son than as a danger to be managed, and who has drawn the leash in accordingly.
characters.name: King Maxim Maresh

characters.description: The queen of Red London and Rhy's mother, whose fondness for Kell has cooled into something closer to fear since her son nearly died.
characters.name: Queen Emira Maresh

characters.description: A young royal guard assigned to the prince, good-natured and devout, who takes Rhy's safety a good deal more personally than the posting requires.
characters.name: Hastra

characters.description: The elder of the two Veskan royals sent to Red London for the tournament: large, physical, openly competitive, and pleased to be somewhere he can prove it.
characters.name: Prince Col

characters.description: The younger Veskan royal, small, cheerful and considerably sharper than the people around her assume. She is very interested in the Arnesian prince, and asks him a great many friendly questions.
characters.name: Princess Cora

characters.description: One of the celebrated Arnesian competitors in the tournament and a favorite of the crowds, with a considerable following in the city before the first match is fought.
characters.name: Kisimyr Vasrin

characters.description: A Veskan competitor in the tournament, a wind magician with a light, showy style that makes him popular with spectators.
characters.name: Jinnar

recaps.ending: The tournament ends in disaster instead of a ceremony. Ojka lures Kell away from the arena and very nearly kills him before Lila reaches them and kills her instead. Holland then takes Kell himself and drags him through to White London, because what Osaron needs is an Antari, and Kell's blood will open a door into a living world. In the palace, Rhy is stabbed in the chaos and does not die, because he cannot while Kell lives, and the carefully kept secret of what Kell did to save him is no longer safe. Lila's own nature is now known to Kell and Alucard: she is Antari, the third of them, self-taught and largely untrained. She forces Alucard to turn the Night Spire toward White London to go after Kell. The book closes with Kell a prisoner in the world he was warned about, Rhy wounded on a throne he has not inherited, Holland restored and no longer anyone's servant, and Osaron poised to cross into a living city.
recaps.in_short: Four months after the black stone, Kell is a restricted, resented royal messenger and Rhy, unkillable while Kell lives, is staging a great international magicians' tournament in Red London. Lila Bard has joined the privateer crew of Captain Alucard Emery, learning the sea and hiding how fast her magic is growing. In Black London, Holland is found half-dead by Osaron, the living magic of that dead world, and takes its bargain: it makes him whole, restores White London to life, and puts him on its throne, in exchange for a way into a living world. Holland sends his agent Ojka after Kell. In Red London, Kell enters the tournament in disguise and so does Lila, and their secrets come apart in front of each other: Lila is Antari too. The tournament is broken up by an attack. Lila kills Ojka, but Holland takes Kell through to White London to use his blood as a doorway, and Rhy is stabbed and survives only because of the bond. Lila and Alucard sail for White London.

recaps.text: Previously: four Londons occupy the same point in different worlds, and only Antari, marked by one solid black eye, can travel between them. Kell, raised in the Red London palace as the crown's messenger, was handed a black stone that turned out to be a piece of Black London, the world magic consumed and which was sealed away centuries ago. Hunted for it, he was robbed of it in Grey London by a street thief named Delilah Bard, and the two of them ended up carrying it back toward its source together. The rulers of White London, the twins Athos and Astrid Dane, wanted the stone for their starving world; they kept the only other living Antari, Holland, bound to their service by a spell cut into his skin. Lila killed Athos and Kell broke Holland's binding, but Astrid had already crossed into Red London and taken Prince Rhy's body. Kell destroyed her, which meant killing his brother, then tied his own life to Rhy's with Antari blood magic to bring him back. Rhy now cannot die while Kell lives, and the two of them share pain. Kell bound the stone into the dying Holland, pushed him through the door into Black London and sealed it. Lila, refusing a comfortable place in a magical world, left for a ship of her own.

Four months on, Lila Bard is at sea.
